h1: AI chatbot for customer support: what it does and how it connects to your helpdesk
description: How an AI chatbot for customer support answers FAQs, collects details and hands off to agents — and how it connects to Zendesk or Freshdesk via API.
keyFacts: Zendesk AI agents generate replies from connected knowledge sources and fall back to a default reply when nothing relevant is found.
Freshdesk AI Agents can transfer a conversation to a human automatically when the customer uses phrases the admin has listed.
A third-party bot in Zendesk messaging hands over by passing control to the Agent Workspace, which makes the conversation eligible for assignment.

navLabel: AI voice bot for phone support
h1: AI voice bot for customer service: how inbound voice automation works
description: How an AI voice bot for customer service works: telephony, speech-to-text, AI logic and text-to-speech, plus call transfer, IVR vs. bot and FCC rules.
keyFacts: A traditional IVR works with keypresses (DTMF); Twilio's Gather verb defaults to DTMF and must be set to accept speech to transcribe callers.
Twilio's bidirectional Media Streams carry call audio as 8 kHz, single-channel mu-law, base64-encoded over a WebSocket.
Zendesk lets an external voice AI agent answer calls first and escalate to a live agent over a SIP-IN line.

h1: Ticket routing automation: methods, tools and setup
description: Ticket routing automation explained: rule-based, round-robin, load-based and skills-based routing, AI triage, and how Zendesk, Freshdesk and Jira do it.
keyFacts: Zendesk omnichannel routing assigns by default to the agent with the most spare capacity; round robin is the alternative method.
Freshdesk's Omniroute engine powers its round-robin, load-based and skill-based ticket assignment.
Jira automation's assign action can distribute work by balanced workload, round-robin or random selection.

h1: Automated customer support reporting: metrics, schedules and delivery
description: Automated customer support reporting: which metrics to track and how to schedule reports from Zendesk, Freshdesk or Jira to email, Slack or Google Sheets.
keyFacts: Zendesk Explore can email a shared dashboard on a recurring schedule set up to 12 months ahead.
In Freshdesk Analytics, custom reports can be scheduled; curated reports must be cloned first.
Jira filter subscriptions email saved search results on a schedule, including cron-based timing; only the first 200 results are sent.

h1: Customer support email automation: from inbox to answered ticket
description: Customer support email automation: forward your support address into Zendesk or Freshdesk, set up SPF and DKIM, then acknowledge, route and escalate emails.
keyFacts: Every Zendesk account has a system support address in the form support@yoursubdomain.zendesk.com.
Zendesk recommends automatic forwarding at the mail server level rather than forwarding from an email client.
Freshdesk converts forwarded email into tickets only once the forwarding rule is in place; Gmail and Microsoft 365 mailboxes can also be connected directly.

h1: AI knowledge base for customer support: how it works and how to build one
description: How an AI knowledge base for customer support works, how to structure articles in Zendesk, Freshdesk or Confluence, keep them current and measure deflection.
keyFacts: Retrieval-augmented generation finds relevant passages in your documents and adds them to the prompt, so the model answers from your content.
In a Zendesk help center, articles live in sections inside categories; they can't sit directly in a category.
Freshdesk organizes its knowledge base into categories, folders and articles.

h1: Zendesk automation: triggers, automations, macros and routing
description: How Zendesk automation works: triggers vs automations vs macros, hourly runs, trigger order, omnichannel and skills routing, webhooks and the Zendesk API.
keyFacts: Ticket triggers run immediately after a ticket is created or updated, in the order they are listed.
Automations run once every hour on non-closed tickets, and each one can act on up to 1,000 tickets per hour.
Every automation needs a condition that is true only once, or an action that nullifies a condition, or it keeps firing.

h1: Freshdesk automation: rule types, assignment and webhooks
description: How Freshdesk automation works: Ticket Creation, Ticket Updates and Hourly Triggers rules, round-robin and skill-based assignment, webhooks and the API.
keyFacts: Freshdesk has three automation rule types: Ticket Creation, Ticket Updates and Hourly Triggers.
Hourly Triggers (formerly Time Triggers) run every hour, on calendar hours, and only on tickets updated in the last 30 days.
Ticket Creation rules can execute either the first matching rule or all matching rules.

h1: Jira Service Management automation: how flows, SLAs and webhooks work
description: How Jira Service Management automation works: triggers, conditions and actions, SLA and approval triggers, smart values, webhooks, queues and request types.
keyFacts: Every automation flow is a trigger, optional conditions, and one or more actions, run top to bottom.
Jira Service Management adds triggers such as 'SLA threshold breached' and 'Approval required'.
The 'Send web request' action calls external systems; an incoming webhook trigger lets external systems start a flow.

h1: Slack customer support automation: alerts, escalations and customer channels
description: Slack customer support automation: escalation alerts, Workflow Builder, incoming webhooks, Bolt apps, Zendesk, Freshdesk and Jira integrations, Slack Connect.
keyFacts: Workflow Builder workflows can start from a link, a webhook, a schedule, a posted message, an emoji reaction or a channel join.
An incoming webhook is a unique URL tied to one channel; you POST a JSON payload to it to post a message.
Slack generally allows apps to post no more than one message per second per channel.

h1: Intercom automation: Workflows, assignment, Fin and the API
description: How Intercom automation works: Workflows triggers, branches and actions, team inbox assignment, Fin AI Agent, Slack and Jira, webhooks and the REST API.
keyFacts: Workflows are built in a visual builder and can be customer-facing or run silently in the background for teammates.
With branches, a conversation follows only the first matching path; Apply rules runs every matched path.
Only one SLA can be applied to a conversation; later SLA actions from other workflows are ignored.

h1: HubSpot Service Hub automation: help desk, tickets, workflows and the API
description: HubSpot Service Hub automation: help desk channels and routing, ticket pipelines and statuses, SLA goals, ticket workflows, chatbots, webhooks and the API.
keyFacts: By default, help desk creates tickets automatically from every channel you connect to it.
The default Support Pipeline has four ticket statuses: New, Waiting on contact, Waiting on us and Closed.
Help desk SLA goals can track time to first reply, time to next reply and time to close.

h1: WhatsApp customer support bot: how it works and what Meta allows
description: How a WhatsApp customer support bot works: Business Platform vs app, the 24-hour window, templates, opt-in, pricing basics and connecting to your helpdesk.
keyFacts: When a customer messages or calls you, a 24-hour customer service window opens and resets with each new message.
Inside the window you can send free-form service messages without pre-approval.
Outside the window, templates are the only message type you can send.

h1: Telegram support bot: how it works and how to set it up
description: How to run a Telegram support bot: BotFather setup, webhooks vs long polling, inline keyboards, privacy mode in groups, sending limits and helpdesk handoff.
keyFacts: You create a bot and get its authentication token by messaging @BotFather.
Updates arrive through getUpdates or a webhook; the two methods are mutually exclusive.
Telegram keeps undelivered updates for no longer than 24 hours.

h1: Facebook Messenger bot for customer service: windows, tags and handoff
description: How a Facebook Messenger bot for customer service works: webhooks, the 24-hour window, the HUMAN_AGENT tag, handover to live agents and Meta's bot policy.
keyFacts: Standard messaging lets you respond within 24 hours of a person's message.
The HUMAN_AGENT tag allows human replies within 7 days, after app approval.
Since April 27, 2026, the CONFIRMED_EVENT_UPDATE, ACCOUNT_UPDATE and POST_PURCHASE_UPDATE tags return an error.

h1: Instagram DM automation for customer support
description: Instagram DM automation explained: professional account rules, the 24-hour window, the human agent tag, comment-to-DM private replies and ice breakers.
keyFacts: Instagram's messaging APIs work with professional accounts (business or creator).
Your app can message a user only after they message you, then has 24 hours to respond.
The human agent tag allows replies within 7 days, after app review.

h1: Website chatbot for customer support: widgets, handoff and accessibility
description: Plan a website chatbot for customer support: helpdesk widgets like Zendesk and Freshchat, bot-to-agent handoff, after-hours coverage and WCAG accessibility.
keyFacts: Zendesk's messaging Web Widget is installed by adding a code snippet to each page where it should appear.
Zendesk messaging can show different responses during and outside business hours.
Freshdesk AI agents can be set to collect customer details before transferring to a human.

h1: SMS customer support automation: how it works and what to set up
description: How SMS customer support automation works: inbound webhooks, A2P 10DLC and toll-free verification, STOP opt-outs, segment limits and helpdesk tickets.
keyFacts: Twilio sends each incoming text to your webhook URL with fields such as From, To, Body and MessageSid.
Twilio says US carriers treat any message sent from a platform like Twilio as application-to-person (A2P) traffic.
Messages from unregistered US 10DLC numbers are blocked with error 30034, even while registration is pending.

h1: Viber chatbot for customer support: how it works and how to set it up
description: How a Viber chatbot for customer support works: auth token, set_webhook, callback events, who the bot can message, keyboards and handoff to your helpdesk.
keyFacts: Every API request carries the bot's authentication token in the X-Viber-Auth-Token header.
Webhook URLs must use SSL; Viber doesn't support self-signed certificates.
The message, subscribed and unsubscribed callbacks are mandatory and can't be filtered out.

h1: What is customer support automation?
description: What customer support automation is: bots, routing, macros, auto-replies, SLA timers and reports, what should stay human, and how it plugs into your helpdesk.
keyFacts: Zendesk triggers run immediately after a ticket is created or updated; Zendesk automations are time-based and run once every hour.
Zendesk macros have no conditions: an agent decides when to apply one.
Zendesk, Freshdesk and Jira automation can all send HTTP requests to other systems from their rules.

h1: Chatbot to human handoff: how to escalate without losing the customer
description: How chatbot to human handoff works: when to escalate, what context to pass to agents, after-hours fallbacks, and how Zendesk, Freshdesk and Messenger do it.
keyFacts: Zendesk says an AI agent may need to transfer a query to a human when it is complex, urgent or sensitive.
Freshdesk AI Agents can transfer automatically when a customer uses trigger phrases you define, such as asking for an agent.
In Dialogflow CX, if no intent meets the classification threshold, a no-match event fires instead of a match.

h1: Customer support metrics: what to track and how each is calculated
description: Customer support metrics explained: first response time, resolution time, FCR, reopens, CSAT, CES, NPS and backlog, with how each one is actually calculated.
keyFacts: Zendesk's full resolution time runs from ticket creation to the ticket's most recent solve, so reopened tickets keep counting.
Freshdesk counts a ticket toward FCR only if the customer sent no further messages after first contacting you.
NPS is the percentage of promoters (scores 9–10) minus the percentage of detractors (scores 0–6).

h1: SLA policies in customer support, explained
description: SLA policies in customer support: first reply, next reply and resolution targets, business vs calendar hours, pausing, breach alerts, and helpdesk setup.
keyFacts: Zendesk applies the first SLA policy, from the top of the list down, whose conditions a ticket matches.
In Zendesk, requester wait time pauses in Pending, and agent work time pauses in Pending and On-hold.
Freshdesk lets you calculate each SLA in business hours or calendar hours (24x7).

h1: Ticket deflection: what it is and how to measure it honestly
description: Ticket deflection explained: which self-service channels deflect, how Zendesk, Freshdesk and Intercom measure it, and why abandoned sessions inflate the rate.
keyFacts: Zendesk's self-service score, also called the ticket deflection ratio, compares help center usage with tickets created in the same period.
Zendesk records an assumed deflection when a help center visitor submits no ticket but never confirms they found an answer.
In Zendesk's AI agent reports, any conversation that doesn't end in escalation counts as deflected.

h1: Omnichannel customer support: what it means and how it works
description: Omnichannel customer support explained: how it differs from multichannel, unified agent workspaces, omnichannel routing, and WhatsApp and Messenger windows.
keyFacts: Freshworks describes multichannel support as independent channels that each operate autonomously; in omnichannel support they are interconnected.
In the Zendesk Agent Workspace, a single ticket conversation can include email, chat and voice.
Zendesk's omnichannel routing assigns email, messaging and call tickets based on agent status and spare capacity.

h1: n8n vs Make vs Zapier for support automation
description: n8n vs Make vs Zapier for support automation: licensing and hosting, how each counts usage, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Jira and Slack connectors, webhooks, code.
keyFacts: n8n's self-hosted software uses the Sustainable Use License, a fair-code license n8n created in 2022. n8n does not call itself open source.
As of October 2026, n8n counts executions (one workflow run), Make counts credits (operations converted 1:1) and Zapier counts tasks (successful action steps).
Zapier triggers, Filter steps and Paths steps don't use tasks. Make trigger modules use 1 credit per run even when they find no new data.

h1: EU AI Act chatbot rules: what Article 50 requires and when
description: EU AI Act chatbot rules explained: what Article 50 requires, who counts as provider or deployer, key dates, and what the 2026 Digital Omnibus on AI changed.
keyFacts: Article 50(1): providers must make sure people are informed that they're interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the context.
Article 50(5): the information must be given in a clear and distinguishable way, at the latest at the first interaction.
The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024. Article 50 applies from 2 August 2026.

h1: GDPR and customer support automation: a practical guide
description: GDPR and customer support automation: lawful bases, data minimisation, retention and processor agreements, applied to chatbots and helpdesk workflows.
keyFacts: Article 5(1)(c): personal data must be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the purposes.
Article 6(1) lists six lawful bases. The EU Court of Justice treats the list as exhaustive.
Article 28(3) requires a binding contract with each processor, including that it acts only on your documented instructions.

h1: European Accessibility Act and customer service: what support teams need to know
description: European Accessibility Act customer service guide: which services are in scope, key dates, the microenterprise exemption and what Annex I asks of support.
keyFacts: Article 31: Member States had to adopt their national laws by 28 June 2022 and apply them from 28 June 2025.
Article 2(2) covers services to consumers such as electronic communications, consumer banking, e-books and e-commerce.
Article 4(5) exempts microenterprises providing services; Article 3(23) defines them as fewer than 10 persons with turnover or balance sheet total of EUR 2 million or less.

h1: n8n Zendesk integration: nodes, credentials and example workflows
description: n8n Zendesk integration guide: Zendesk node operations, the Zendesk Trigger, OAuth2 credentials and the end of API tokens, webhooks, rate limits, an example.
keyFacts: The n8n Zendesk node has four resources: Ticket, Ticket Field, User and Organization.
Setting tags with the node's Update Ticket operation replaces the whole tag list. Tags you leave out are removed.
n8n's Zendesk credential supports OAuth2 or an API token, but Zendesk stopped issuing new API tokens on October 27, 2026 and switches all of them off on April 30, 2027.

h1: Attio workflows: how CRM automation works in Attio
description: Attio workflows explained: trigger and action blocks, how workflow credits are used, REST API rate limits, webhook signatures and ways to link Attio to support.
keyFacts: An Attio workflow is built from a trigger block, which starts it, and action blocks, which do the work.
Triggers, logic and data lookups are free. Blocks that write data, call outside systems or use AI use workspace credits, most of them one credit per run.
Attio's REST API allows 100 read requests and 25 write requests per second. Over the limit it returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.

h1: Attio vs HubSpot automation: workflows, limits, API and webhooks
description: Attio vs HubSpot automation compared: who gets workflows, limits and credits, triggers, code and webhook steps, API rate limits and webhook signature checks.
keyFacts: HubSpot workflows need a Professional or Enterprise subscription. Marketing, Sales or Service Hub Professional allows up to 300 workflows, and Enterprise up to 1,000.
Attio meters workflows with workspace credits. Triggers, logic and lookups are free, and most blocks that write data or call out use one credit per run.
HubSpot custom code actions must finish within 20 seconds and can use up to 128 MB of memory. Attio's 'Execute code' block times out after 100 seconds.

h1: HubSpot Zendesk integration: what syncs, what doesn't and your options
description: HubSpot Zendesk integration guide: what the free Zendesk for HubSpot app syncs and doesn't, action flows, two-way sync apps and custom builds with both APIs.
keyFacts: The Zendesk Support for HubSpot integration is one-way: ticket information flows from Zendesk to HubSpot.
It creates three Zendesk triggers, for new tickets, solved tickets and CSAT ratings, plus a webhook called HubSpot Integration.
Tickets appear only on the HubSpot contact timeline, not on companies or deals, and only the user's email address is synced.

h1: AI lead scoring: how scoring against your ICP works
description: AI lead scoring explained: scoring leads against your ideal customer profile, HubSpot's lead scoring tool and limits, and writing scores to Attio via API.
keyFacts: HubSpot's lead scoring tool needs Marketing Hub or Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise; AI-built contact scores need Marketing Hub Enterprise.
HubSpot's AI lead scores need a minimum sample of 50 contacts — 25 converted and 25 non-converted — before a score can be generated.
Attio has no built-in scoring engine or score field type: a score lives in a number or select attribute that a workflow or the API fills.

h1: Website visitor identification: how it works and its limits
description: How website visitor identification works: reverse IP lookup and trackers, what it can and can't see, GDPR and cookie consent rules, and HubSpot buyer intent.
keyFacts: Identification combines a tracking script, tracking cookies, reverse IP lookup, private databases and machine learning — matching visits to companies, not to individual people.
Dealfront's Leadfeeder explicitly refuses to publish a typical identification rate: coverage varies by audience, and visits from consumer ISPs are filtered out and not shown.
Remote workers are mainly identifiable when they browse through a company VPN.
